subject: RFP — Commercial appendix: commit gating, surge buffer & overage mechanics
messages:
From: Sara Long <sara.long@greengrid.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@greengrid.com>, procurement@greengrid.com
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: GreenGrid RFP — commercial appendix questions

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the quick turnaround on the functional fit. We're now working through the commercial appendix (attached: GreenGrid_RFP_Appendix_C.pdf) and have a few clarifying questions specifically on commit/overage mechanics and how Redwood handles short-duration spikes. Procurement asked us to surface three items before the pricing team completes their evaluation:

1) Commit gating: for an annual committed token volume, do you support a staged/earned commit (i.e., portion of the commit vests after each quarter), and if so how are unused committed tokens treated on a quarterly true-up?
2) Spike protection / "surge buffer": can Redwood provide an automated buffer that absorbs short-term spikes (e.g., up to X% of daily usage above baseline) without immediate overage billing? If yes, how does that interact with billing and capacity guarantees?
3) Overage step-downs: if we breach the commit often, do overage rates reduce as cumulative overages increase (volume discounts on overage), or are overages billed at a flat incremental rate?

We'd appreciate a short written response that we can include in our procurement appendix; if easier, happy to take a 30-minute call this week.

Thanks,
Sara Long
Director, Automation & AI
GreenGrid Energy

Attachment: GreenGrid_RFP_Appendix_C.pdf (1 page summary)
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: GreenGrid RFP — commercial appendix questions

Sara —

Appreciate the clear list. Below are concise answers you can paste into the RFP appendix; I've also attached a one-page commercial summary (Redwood_GG_Commercial_Proposal_v1.pdf) and our pricing workbook for transparency. If helpful I can jump on a call Thursday morning PST.

(1) Commit gating / vesting model
- Redwood supports both annual pre-paid commits and staged/earned commits. By default we recommend an annual commit with quarterly milestone vesting (25% vest at the end of each quarter) for new production deployments.
- Unused committed tokens at quarter-end are applied to the next quarter's consumption within the contract year. At year-end any remaining committed tokens are true-upped per the contract (either credited against next year's commit or billed at the overage rate depending on the negotiated option).
- Optional add-on: prorated rollover for the first two quarters (common in pilots) for customers that need softer ramp protections.

(2) Spike protection ("surge buffer")
- We offer a configurable spike buffer that automatically absorbs short-duration spikes up to a defined window. Typical configuration: daily spike buffer = 35% above 24-hour baseline sustained for up to 6 hours; monthly cap protects against persistent over-consumption.
- Billing: buffered spike usage is NOT billed as immediate overage if it falls inside the configured buffer window. Buffered usage is deducted from a separate surge allowance ledger; if the ledger is exhausted, excess is billed at overage rates.
- Capacity guarantees: buffer consumption is best-effort in hosted mode but guaranteed in Redwood Dedicated when reserved capacity is purchased and configured; for Dedicated we include SLA-backed headroom policies and preemption fallbacks.

(3) Overage step-downs
- Overage is billed at an incremental flat rate by default. We can introduce volume-tiering for overages as a negotiated concession (e.g., first 10% overage billed at standard overage rate, 10-30% at -10%, >30% at -20%) for multi-year commitments.
- For strategic pilots and early adoption we propose a staged overage ladder with decreasing marginal price and a cap to limit runaway spend.

Proposed next steps (if GreenGrid wants to proceed):
- Redwood provides a draft commercial appendix with two options: (A) standard annual commit + buffer (hosted); (B) Dedicated reserved capacity with SLA & guaranteed spike headroom.
- If you prefer, we can run a 2-week pilot at a discounted commit (25% off list on the first 250k tokens) to validate baseline and calibrate buffer sizing.

I copied Ben (pricing) and Karthik (legal) — Ben, can you flag any pricing ranges we should put in the appendix and confirm the suggested buffer defaults?

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Sales Manager, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Priya / Karthik —

Quick notes from pricing that I'd include in the final appendix (keeping language procurement-friendly):

- Base token pricing: $0.0009 / token for generation tokens; embedding/tokenized retrieval priced separately per 1k vectors. (We can provide per-model micro-pricing in the workbook.)
- Commit tiers: recommend a 12-month commit with quarterly vesting as you suggested. For GreenGrid size, propose the following bands: 0-10M tokens (list), 10-50M (-7% to -12% discount), 50M+ (-13% to -20% discount) tied to annualized commit.
- Spike buffer mechanics: offer 35% daily buffer, 6-hour sustained window. Buffer ledger starts at 1% of annual commit and is replenished monthly proportional to usage patterns (more conservative than our default).
- Overage ladder option (optional concession): first 10% overage billed at standard overage price; 10-25% billed at -8%; >25% billed at -15% (caps to be mutually agreed). This structure reduces procurement risk while keeping economic incentives.

Notes: if GreenGrid wants guaranteed buffer we should push for Dedicated with a small reserved pool (e.g., mated nodes representing 15-20% headroom) so we can include firm SLA credits if preemption occurs.

I'll attach a distilled pricing worksheet (redwood-pricing-workbook.xlsx) to the appendix we send.

Ben
Director, Commercial Pricing
Redwood Inference

Sara —

Thanks for the quick review window. Attached is a one-page commercial appendix and our transparent pricing workbook. Summary of the final positions we recommend you include in the RFP response:

- Commit model: 12-month annualized commit with quarterly vesting (25% quarterly). Unused quarterly commit rolls forward within the contract year; year-end true-up options: credit toward next-year commit OR billed at negotiated overage ladder.
- Surge buffer: default hosted buffer = 35% above daily baseline for up to a 6-hour sustained event; buffer consumption draws from a surge allowance ledger that resets monthly. Dedicated customers can opt for guaranteed headroom with SLA credits.
- Overage: default flat incremental overage at $0.0012 / token. Optional overage ladder available as a negotiated concession (example bands provided in the attached workbook).
- Pilot offer: 2-week validation pilot at 25% off list for the first 250k tokens to calibrate baseline and buffer sizing; no penalty for scaling into a commit within 30 days of pilot end.

Next steps: if that aligns with GreenGrid's procurement preferences we'll prepare a short addendum showing both (A) hosted option with buffer and (B) Dedicated reserved capacity with guaranteed headroom and SLA language.
